issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal): boolean, but the provided solution implements addAnimal as void and the template does not provide an implementation. This mismatch between the UML and actual/expected method signature can confuse students about the correct return type to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the expected signature consistent across all artifacts. Either update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare addAnimal(animal: Animal): void (and update any textual description if needed), or change the template and solution to implement addAnimal returning boolean (e.g., return true when the add succeeds). Preferably update the UML to :void to match the textual task description and the solution approach, or if a boolean is desired, implement and document the boolean return in template and tests.

issues.description: The UML and task text describe Farm having an aggregation field animals: List<Animal>, but the template Farm.java does not declare this attribute (the field is missing). The solution contains private List<Animal> animals. The absence of this attribute in the template is a structural omission that prevents students from following the intended design.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the animals field to the template Farm.java: declare private List<Animal> animals; initialize it in a no-argument constructor (new ArrayList<>()), and provide the getter and setter as described. This will align the template with the UML and the solution and give students the expected starting structure.

issues.description: The UML and solution define a private singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal): void helper that prints a verse for a specific animal, but the template declares singFarmSongVerse with the Animal parameter commented out (no parameter). This prevents students from implementing the per-animal verse logic as specified.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the parameter in the template: change the method signature to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) and implement the verse using the passed-in animal (animal.getClass().getSimpleName() and animal.messageOnFeed()). This aligns the template with the UML and the provided solution.
